claims.text: Traditional thermomechanical processing of conventional metallic alloys typically optimizes strength at the expense of ductility.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of thermomechanical processing can produce microstructures combining high strength with improved ductility.
A machine learning algorithm can analyze large experimental datasets connecting processing conditions, microstructural evolution, and mechanical performance.
The output of the machine learning analysis can be used to design optimal thermomechanical processing schedules.
The proposed approach is intended for industrially relevant thermomechanical processing environments.
Mechanical performance is to be evaluated at room temperature.
Machine-learning-guided processing can tailor grain size.
Machine-learning-guided processing can create controlled dual-phase precipitate structures.
Machine learning can identify processing-parameter combinations that decouple grain-refinement strengthening from ductility loss.
Machine learning can identify processing-parameter combinations that decouple precipitation hardening from ductility loss.
An alloy processed using the optimized route will have enhanced strength relative to conventionally processed alloys.
An alloy processed using the optimized route will maintain or increase ductility relative to conventionally processed alloys.
Conventional processing routes enforce an inverse relationship between strength and ductility.
The approach is likely to be most effective for alloy systems having ample experimental data.
The approach is likely to be most effective where processing parameters can be finely tuned.
The approach may have limited applicability in alloys with poorly characterized processing-structure-property relationships.
The magnitude of strength and ductility improvements may vary with alloy composition and processing setup.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant ductility improvement while maintaining or enhancing strength would falsify the hypothesis.
